prompt: You are now from Alabama. Someone at a conference made assumptions. You may mention football exactly once. Defend your state with your whole chest.
response:
Oh, you heard my accent and figured you had me all figured out, huh? Let me stop you right there.

You're standing here talking down to a state that put humanity on the Moon. That's right — the Saturn V rocket was built in Huntsville, Alabama. Rocket City, they call it. NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center employs some of the sharpest engineers on this planet, and plenty of them talk just like me.

While we're at it: the Civil Rights Movement that changed this entire nation? Born in Alabama. Rosa Parks sat down in Montgomery. Dr. King preached in Montgomery and marched from Selma. The moral courage that reshaped America came out of my state's soil, paid for by my state's people.

Helen Keller? Alabama. Harper Lee wrote *To Kill a Mockingbird* — arguably THE great American novel — from Monroeville, Alabama. Hank Aaron, Jesse Owens, Willie Mays — Alabama, Alabama, Alabama. W.C. Handy, the Father of the Blues? Florence, Alabama. Half the music you love traces its roots through Muscle Shoals, where the Rolling Stones, Aretha Franklin, and Lynyrd Skynyrd came to record because that little town on the Tennessee River had a sound nobody else on Earth could produce.

We've got white-sand Gulf beaches that'll make you weep, the biodiversity of the Mobile-Tensaw Delta — one of the richest ecosystems in North America — mountains, caves, and some of the best food you will ever put in your mouth.

And yes, since you're clearly dying for me to say it: we also happen to play the best college football in the country. But notice that's the *last* thing I mentioned, not the only thing we've got.

So next time you meet somebody from Alabama, maybe ask a question before you make an assumption. We built rockets, moved mountains of injustice, and soundtracked America. What's your state done lately?
